verdict.rationale: Bolt documents connecting a GitHub repository that automatically backs up the project with full history, syncs commits, supports branches, and can create a new repo from a Bolt project or import an existing repo. However, the evidence never explicitly says that changes made directly in GitHub flow back into an existing Bolt project; import is shown only as a one-time load. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of GitHub-to-Bolt pull or two-way sync for an existing project, and independent hands-on corroboration of the sync behavior.

support.subject: As a developer, I can sync my project to my own GitHub repository and keep changes flowing both ways

citations.quote: Connect a GitHub repository to back up your Bolt project, sync commits automatically, and work across branches.
Connecting GitHub to Bolt lets you automatically back up your Bolt project with a full history of changes that lives outside Bolt.
Create a new repository from a Bolt project
Import a GitHub repository. Load an existing repository as a Bolt project.
